note: Token-matched billing arms run 2026-10-04, after the cpa-usage plugin (docs/relay/usage-oracle.md) made per-request token counts readable. Tokens are the plugin's own per-request record. The meter is the upstream's integer 5h/weekly percent, read live per account by billing_probe.py. Account emails are replaced by the same acct-N labels billing_probe.py uses (acct-1 k12, acct-2 plus, acct-3 plus). No prompt or response text is recorded here: only counts, sizes and timings.

meter.kind: upstream used_percent, integer, 5h window (primary) and weekly window (secondary)
meter.resolution: 1 point; a delta below that is not observable, so the abort arm's cost is an upper bound

cost_model_2026-10-05.what: The 5h/weekly percent is a spend meter, not a token counter: points = a*uncached_input + b*cache_read + c*output, least-squares over the six windows where every finalized request is attributable and the meter delta is bracketed by two reads. Token classes are the plugin's own per-request record; 'cache_read' is the plugin's cache_read_tokens.
cost_model_2026-10-05.rounded_for_use: 1 point is about 10,500 uncached input tokens, or 2,000 output tokens, or 105,000 cache-read tokens -- at gpt-6-astra's price. Other models are priced differently: see per_model_factors.

windows.window: H2 warm-direct, 10 x the same 60k body
H3 out-direct, 3 tiny prompts with long answers

cost_model_2026-10-05.reading: A cache read is charged at about a tenth of an uncached input token and an output token at about five times one, at gpt-6-astra's price. The nine-window fit has RMS 0.798; forcing cache reads free costs 1.509, forcing them to par 11.500, and forcing output free 2.870. The flat claim that 'cached input is charged' was right about the sign and wrong about the price by implying par; 'cache reads are free' is rejected. The individual coefficients are correlated and only the ratios are robust.
cost_model_2026-10-05.limits: One plan (plus), one account for the campaign arms, nine windows, RMS 0.798; the cache coefficient is pinned to 0.10x-0.19x (0.053x-0.129x by leave-one-out) and the coefficients are correlated. A per-request term is not separable at a 1-point resolution. The aborted path is measured only through the meter, because an aborted request has no oracle event at all -- which is exactly why 'no event' cannot be read as 'no charge'. Per-model factors are measured for three models only, each from a small number of requests.
cost_model_2026-10-05.status: Fitted 2026-10-05 on the six 2026-10-04 arms (1/10,034-1/74,593-1/2,557, RMS 0.713), corrected the same day for the arm S row, then refitted the same night on nine controlled windows after a single-account campaign with 35-minute settles added H1 cold-direct, H2 warm-direct and H3 out-direct. The campaign also measured per-model prices (terra 0.214x, luna ~0) and one relayed owner-body arm that settled +5 with zero usage events -- see campaign_2026-10-05.

identifiability.method: leave-one-out over the nine windows, plus forcing one term at a time with the others refitted
identifiability.uncached_input: 1/10,112 to 1/11,013 tokens per point (the fit is 1/10,538)
identifiability.cache_read: 1/78,160 to 1/196,625 tokens per point -- the weakest coefficient. Dropping H3 moves it to 1/78,160 (0.129x of the uncached coefficient), dropping arm G-A to 1/196,625 (0.053x). The fit is 1/104,896 = 0.100x.
identifiability.output: 1/1,920 to 1/2,897 tokens per point (the fit is 1/2,055 = 5.13x the uncached coefficient); the two output-dominated windows on their own (H3, and the 13:20 natural experiment) imply about 1/1,900 each
identifiability.correlation: the arms' input:output ratios are similar enough that a and c trade against each other and the cache term trades against both. The defensible claims are the ratios, not the individual tokens-per-point.
identifiability.rejections_over_the_nine: cache reads free (b=0) RMS 1.509 with the other coefficients frozen, 1.244 with them refitted; cache reads at par (b=a) 11.500 frozen, 5.858 refitted; output free (c=0) 2.870 frozen, 1.899 refitted; the fit 0.798. Both columns reject all three; the earlier version of the doc printed only the frozen column while calling it refitted, which a reader pass caught.
identifiability.arm_S_correction: the arm S row first read unc 1,715 / out 3,025 / predicted 1.50, because arm S's recorded window ends '09:11:41Z' and its sixth astra event is at 09:11:41.324313Z -- inside the same second, outside a whole-second inclusive comparison. Corrected to 2,057 / 3,628 by a reader pass.
identifiability.what_would_pin_it: a cache-warm direct arm at the same total input volume as a cache-cold one, on one account, in one window. H2 against H1 is that arm; it moved the cache coefficient from 0.135x to 0.100x and made b=0 cost RMS 1.51 against 0.80.

per_model_factors.what: the meter is a multi-model spend meter: the same token counts cost different numbers of points depending on the model. All coefficients above are gpt-6-astra's price.

gpt-5.6-terra.evidence: 3 finalized requests of 28,659 / 28,848 / 28,791 uncached tokens and 664 / 826 / 857 output, no cache, astra-equivalent cost 9.33 points, meter moved +2 both immediately and after the 35-minute settle

per_model_factors.check: the owner's own direct session (14:26-14:30Z; 6 astra + 8 terra + 2 luna events, 446,947 input of which 374,784 cache reads, 72,163 uncached, 8,089 output) predicts 5.97 + 7.78*0.214 + 0.61*0 = 7.63 points and was recorded at +7. Priced as if every model were astra it predicts 14.36.

gpt-6-luna.evidence: the 20-event confound window is 14 gpt-6-luna events worth 17.3 astra-equivalent points against a delta of 0 (bound < 0.06), and the day's 25 gpt-6-luna requests carry 1,195,240 input tokens (150,760 uncached, 1,044,480 cache reads) plus ~5,000 output, worth ~27 astra-equivalent points across the day, with the meters moving only in the astra arms (bound < 0.04)

gpt-5.6-luna.evidence: 2 events, ~18k input tokens, ~0.6 astra-equivalent points -- too little traffic to bound anything; a different model from the gpt-6-luna row

reconciled_2026-10-05.headline: This is a MODEL control, not a cache control, and it is not evidence about the price of a cache read.
reconciled_2026-10-05.why: Of the 20 events, 14 are gpt-6-luna, and luna carries all but 2,057 of the input and ALL 448,256 of the cache reads (the earlier 397,312 was a narrower read of the same window, 09:07:10-09:12:22Z instead of the full 20-event window). Under the fitted cost model (cost_model_2026-10-05) that luna volume is worth 19.4 points and the meter moved by 0. The confound note's own two reads recorded 0 for this window too; arm S's record, whose reads bracket the same traffic more widely, recorded +1 on acct-2, which is inside the ~1.6 points arm S's own six astra requests in the same window predict. Across the whole day 25 gpt-6-luna requests carrying 1,195,240 input tokens of which 1,044,480 were cache reads left the 5h meters flat, while every gpt-6-astra arm moved them.
reconciled_2026-10-05.conclusion: gpt-6-luna usage does not appear in these accounts' 5h/weekly percent at all; the reason is unestablished and does not need to be for the arms to be read. What the note still establishes is that a second client's traffic lands in these accounts and has to be excluded per model, which is why the cost-model fit sums astra events only.
reconciled_2026-10-05.the_earlier_reading: 'charged at a scale more than an order of magnitude below uncached' was wrong in the sense that it treated luna volume as if it were astra volume; the fitted answer is about one eighth, measured on astra windows.

Its bodies are 243 characters, so it bounds nothing about a large aborted body. The same cron fired at 01:05:55Z, inside H4's settle window (last dispatch 00:34:36Z, settle read ~01:09Z): 4 runs, 8 dispatches, ~2.8k chars each, which bounds its contribution to H4's +5 at about one point. H5's window (01:52-02:57Z) had no tripwire arm in it -- that cron fires on odd UTC hours.
campaign_2026-10-05.max_output_tokens: honoured on a four-token smoke prompt and ignored on the 60k bodies (634-775 output tokens each) and on H3 (3,144-3,222), so no arm isolates output by suppression; the fit uses the oracle's own per-request counts.
campaign_2026-10-05.open: A relayed owner-body turn cost the meter about 0.42 points (12 turns -> +5) while a relayed filler arm of larger volume charged about nothing (C-scale-30: 30 turns, 144 dispatches, 4,274,417 aborted tokens -> +2). The two are not reconciled; see the relay-charge section of docs/relay/unbill-benefit.md for what is and is not claimed.

relay_charge_2026-10-05.what: How much a relayed (aborted) client turn costs the meter. Every revision of this repository before this one inferred 'the charge is not incurred' from the absence of a finalized usage event; these arms measure the meter instead.

mechanism_verified.claim: the relay's mid-read close reaches the provider, so the upstream request is terminated and no usage block is ever sent
mechanism_verified.how: arm H4's 20 dispatches appear in cliproxy's own log, and every dispatch ends at or before the end of the relay run that owns it -- 0 of 20 end after every candidate run (the last dispatch ends exactly at the last run's end, 00:34:36Z)
mechanism_verified.trap: cliproxy's log timestamps in UTC+8 while this host runs UTC+7; a first pass that read the log as UTC paired the wrong arms and appeared to show dispatches outliving their runs. It does not.
mechanism_verified.oracle: zero usage events for all 12 runs; all 12 real_completed false

arms.note: measured on two accounts, one of which (acct-3) shows 0% because it was disabled and unreadable, so this is an under-read

arms.id: H5 relay-owner, settled baseline, watched for 55 minutes
arms.note: baseline settled (two reads 4 minutes apart both 38%); +4 already at the +5-minute read and unchanged at +15; no tripwire arm in the window (its cron fires on odd hours); no other /v1/responses traffic in the window per cliproxy's log

arms.id: H4 settle window contains the 01:05:55Z tripwire arm
arms.note: a reader pass caught that H4's +5 is asserted to be its own while the tripwire's abort-only arm also fired inside H4's settle window; its volume bounds the contamination at about one point, and H5 -- whose window is clean of it -- independently measures +4

direct_counterpart.note: the same body, the same 12 turns, straight to cliproxy

relay_charge_2026-10-05.conclusion: 12 relayed turns of the owner's own body cost the meter 4-5 points against 8 for the same 12 turns direct: about 0.33-0.42 points per relayed turn, a saving of roughly 1.6x-2x rather than the >=4x this repository published. The cut removes the usage event, not the charge.

contradiction.what: 30 relayed turns with 60,000-character unique-filler bodies, 144 dispatches, 4,274,417 aborted tokens, moved the pool by +2 on a reading three minutes later, with no other finalized traffic in the window
contradiction.why_it_matters: same construction as H4/H5 with more volume and less charge
contradiction.likely_direction: the charge is probably proportional to the output the provider had already generated when the cut fired, not to the aborted input: a toolpad/toolcall cut fires before much text exists, while a sentinel cut on a real body fires after the model has written. The cut chains are recorded above so this is testable; it is not settled here.
contradiction.resolution: The two bodies differ in whether the provider has a prefix cached to read. The filler bodies are unique random text with no prompt_cache_key, so their dispatches read nothing from cache; the owner's body is cached (a replay of it reported 27,776 of 30,487 input tokens from cache). The aborted charge is the cache-read term of the same fitted spend model, and it prices per dispatch: 0.158-0.21 points on a warm prefix (O6 19 dispatches +3, O1 12 dispatches +2, H5 19 dispatches +4) against a fit prediction of 0.18, and 0.00 over 14 cache-cold dispatches (O6c). The direction recorded in `likely_direction` - that the charge follows the output the provider had already generated - is refuted by the same arms: the cache-cold arm generated and delivered *more* text than the warm one (152.8 against 103.1 characters per turn) and charged nothing.

relay_charge_2026-10-05.oracle_lesson: 'no usage event' is not 'no charge'. The provider can bill the prompt it read and the output it had already generated when the connection dropped, without ever sending a usage block. Any claim of the form 'the cut removes the charge' has to be made against the meter.

continuation_2026-10-05.what: Four arms in one empty 5h window on the single enabled account, to price the relay's continuation and to test whether its charge follows the provider's prefix cache. Same body (the owner's recovered Codex request, 136,577 chars) for C6/O6/O1; O6c differs only in a unique 16-character nonce at the start of the system prompt, so no dispatch of it can be served from cache. 20 turns an arm (10 for O6c), 5 at a time, a meter and oracle read before and after each arm, and a 30-minute settle between them.

arms.note: the cache is busted by a new first developer message, which changes no client item and no tool; `prompt_chars` grows by the marker, so the run log carries the evidence that it ran

prefix_cache_2026-10-05.what: Direct (non-relayed) replays of the owner's recovered Codex body against cliproxy:8317, to measure the provider's prefix cache before attributing any aborted-path charge to it. Six requests, 2026-10-05T03:24-03:39Z, all before the 5h window reset at 03:41:10Z. Counts and timings only; the body itself is not recorded here.
prefix_cache_2026-10-05.reason: The four-arm campaign on the relay prices a continuation and tests whether an aborted dispatch is charged for the cached prefix. That test is only readable if a front-of-request nonce actually makes the provider's cache miss, so the cache behaviour was measured directly first.

requests.reading: first replay of this prefix after >10 minutes idle: cache expired, nothing served from it

the same body again, immediately: 27,776 of 30,487 input tokens (91%) served from the prefix cache. So the provider really does cache this body across requests, and the relay's dispatches are the same prefix

a 16-character nonce prepended to the *system prompt* (input item 1) still matched 9,728 tokens: item 0, the developer additional_tools item, precedes it and stayed cached. This is why the campaign's cold arm puts the nonce in item 0, not item 1
a different nonce in the same place matched exactly the same 9,728 tokens, i.e. the match stops where the nonce is
the nonce in item 0's first nested tool description - the earliest text in the request - served nothing from cache
repeated with another nonce: still 0. The cache is keyed from the first characters, so a front nonce defeats it

the relay-shaped variant: a new first input item instead of a rewrite of the client's own. Accepted by the provider and also 0 cached, which is the implementation to prefer (it never edits the client's content)

prefix_cache_2026-10-05.limits: One model (gpt-6-astra), one account, one body shape, direct path (not through the relay), six requests. The direct path has no injected padding tool and no appended instruction, so these numbers are the provider's cache behaviour for the client prefix; the relay's own additions are measured by the campaign's arms, not here. `input_tokens` is the provider's total with `cached_tokens` a subset of it, which is the class split the spend model uses.

aborted_price_2026-10-05.what: What one aborted dispatch costs, warm and cold, and how it was measured.

O6c.note: nonce in item 0's first tool description, which also changed the model's behaviour

O6c2.note: nonce prepended as an inert developer message; behaviour closer to the warm arm (10 of 12 turns toolpad+sentinel). The 1 point is the meter's own floor over 22 dispatches, and the tripwire's own four-run arm also fired inside this bracket (07:05Z, 8 dispatches of a ~250-character prompt), so this is a ceiling on the cold price rather than a measurement of it; the clean cold reading is O6c's 0 over 14 dispatches

cold_dispatch_points.bound: 22 cache-cold dispatches moved the meter by one point, so the cold price is at most ~0.045 points a dispatch against 0.158-0.21 warm

fit_prediction.how: 136,577 characters is ~22,800 tokens at this document's 5.99 characters per token and 28,333 at the provider's own count on the finalized counterpart of the same body (4.82 characters per token); ~90% cache reads gives 0.9 * 22,800 / 104,896 = 0.18 to 0.9 * 28,333 / 104,896 = 0.24
fit_prediction.tension: the measured warm price (0.158-0.21) sits at the bottom of that band, so either the aborted dispatch's billable prefix is smaller than the finalized request's or its cache share is lower; nothing here separates those

continuation.reading: the continuation is priced like any other dispatch and carries more than half the delivered characters; max_segments=1 removes it and with it most of the answer

day_level.why_it_changed: the day's turns averaged 3.5 dispatches against the arms' 1.6, and the price transfers per dispatch

aborted_price_2026-10-05.limits: one account, one model (gpt-6-astra), one body shape, one 5h window; the meter is an integer percent; the cold arm's nonce changes 16 characters of the request; why the provider charges the cached part of an aborted request and not the fresh part is not observable here.
